The first lesson on this page's loops stayed in major. Minor is different in one important way: the
scale you play on is not the scale the chords come from. Natural minor has no leading tone, so the V
chord is changed to get one. This lesson writes everything in **A minor**.

**How to use the page.** Press ▶ on a chart and the band plays it four times after a one-bar count-in. The bar that is sounding lights up, on the chart and on the staff. Under every chord is its Roman numeral, which stays the same in every key. The strip at the bottom of the window sets the key, the feel, the tempo and the chord instrument, and you can change them while the band plays. Shaded bars are the ones that differ from the version named under the chart.

## 1. The basic minor changes

**Am, Dm, Em, Am**: i, iv, v, i, all from the natural minor scale. The v chord, Em, is minor. It is
pleasant and it is also weak: it has G, not G♯, so there is no leading tone to pull to A.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="basic"></div>

## 2. The harmonic-minor V7

**Am, Dm, E7, Am.** One note changes, G to G♯, and the chord becomes the dominant. The G♯ is the
leading tone and it rises to A. This is the chord that makes minor feel like a key and not a mode.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="harm"></div>

## 3. The Picardy third

**Am, Dm, E7, A.** Finish on a major chord. The C of the A minor chord is raised to C♯. It is an old
trick, for a hymn or a baroque piece: the music goes dark and the last chord turns the lights on.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="pic"></div>

## 4. A walking bass

**Am Am/G | Dm/F Dm | E7 | Am.** The bass steps down A, G, F, then falls a third to D, and E7 and Am follow. The slash chord Am/G is an A minor chord over a G in the
bass.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="walk"></div>

## 5. ii° to V to i

**Am, Dm, Bm7♭5 E7, Am.** Put the half-diminished ii chord in front of the dominant. It is the minor
version of the two-five: B, D, F, A, then E7. The bass falls a fifth from B to E, and again from E to A,
the same circle-of-fifths motion as in the major two-five-one.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="twofive"></div>
